title: _batch_runner.py: source code
body:
# Batch fetcher runner: <=8 HTTP GETs per target, 1s sleep same-host, saves raw/ + scan JSON
import sys, os, json, time, re
from urllib.parse import urljoin
BASE = r"C:\Users\Garrett\.hermes\competitor-intel"
RAW = os.path.join(BASE, "raw")
sys.path.insert(0, BASE)
from fetcher import fetch, RAW as _R  # noqa

VENDORS = ["sportradar", "statsperform", "opta", "genius", "the-odds-api", "sportsdata", "nflverse", "fantasydata", "apidata", "rapidapi"]
JS_GREP = [r"baseURL", r"axios", r"fetch\(", r"endpoint", r"isPremium", r"hasAccess", r"user\.tier", r"subscription", r"subscri", r"monteCarlo", r"numSims", r"simulation", r"correlation", r"localStorage", r"premium"]

def run_target(domain, url_home, prefix, js_max=3):
    recs, store = [], {}
    def get(url, save=None):
        r = fetch(url, save_name=save)
        recs.append({"url": url, "status": r["status"], "error": r["error"], "ms": r["ms"],
                     "bytes": len(r.get("body") or ""),
                     "hdrs": {k: r["headers"].get(k) for k in ("server", "x-powered-by", "cf-ray", "x-vercel-id", "via", "content-type") if r["headers"].get(k)},
                     "saved": r.get("saved")})
        time.sleep(1.0)
        return r
    # 1 homepage
    r = get(url_home, f"{prefix}_home.html")
    html = r.get("body") or ""
    store["home_status"] = r["status"]
    store["home_url"] = url_home
    # robots
    rr = get(urljoin(url_home, "/robots.txt"), f"{prefix}_robots.txt")
    store["robots_status"] = rr["status"]
    store["robots_body"] = (rr.get("body") or "")[:3000]
    sm = re.findall(r"Sitemap:\s*(\S+)", store["robots_body"], re.I)
    store["robots_sitemaps"] = sm
    # sitemap (robots-declared first, else /sitemap.xml)
    smurl = sm[0] if sm else urljoin(url_home, "/sitemap.xml")
    sr = get(smurl, f"{prefix}_sitemap.xml")
    store["sitemap_status"] = sr["status"]
    store["sitemap_url"] = smurl
    sbody = sr.get("body") or ""
    locs = re.findall(r"<loc>\s*([^<\s]+)\s*</loc>", sbody)
    store["sitemap_loc_count"] = len(locs)
    store["sitemap_sample"] = locs[:12]
    # 2 JS bundles from homepage
    srcs = re.findall(r"<script[^>]+src=[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']", html, re.I)
    jurls, seen = [], set()
    for s in srcs:
        u = urljoin(url_home, s)
        if u.endswith((".js", ".mjs")) and u not in seen:
            seen.add(u); jurls.append(u)
    # heuristic: prefer main-ish bundles
    prio = [u for u in jurls if re.search(r"(main|app|index|bundle|chunk|vendor|runtime)", u, re.I)]
    order = (prio + [u for u in jurls if u not in prio])[:js_max]
    store["js_candidates_total"] = len(jurls)
    store["js_fetched"] = []
    greps = {}
    for i, u in enumerate(order):
        rj = get(u, f"{prefix}_js{i}.js")
        store["js_fetched"].append({"url": u, "status": rj["status"], "bytes": len(rj.get("body") or "")})
        body = rj.get("body") or ""
        for pat in JS_GREP + [v for v in VENDORS]:
            for m in re.finditer(pat, body, re.I):
                greps.setdefault(pat, []).append({"file": f"{prefix}_js{i}.js", "ctx": body[max(0, m.start()-70):m.end()+90].replace("\n", " ")[:170]})
                if len(greps[pat]) >= 4: break
    # homepage html greps (vendors, api paths, pricing links)
    for pat in JS_GREP + [v for v in VENDORS]:
        for m in re.finditer(pat, html, re.I):
            greps.setdefault(pat + "_home", []).append({"file": "home.html", "ctx": html[max(0, m.start()-60):m.end()+80].replace("\n", " ")[:150]})
            if len(greps[pat + "_home"]) >= 3: break
    store["greps"] = greps
    plinks = list(dict.fromkeys(urljoin(url_home, h) for h in re.findall(r'href=[\"\']([^\"\']*(?:pricing|subscribe|plans|membership|signup|register)[^\"\']*)[\"\"]?', html, re.I) if "javascript" not in h))[:3]
    store["pricing_links"] = plinks
    if plinks:
        rp = get(plinks[0], f"{prefix}_pricing.html")
        store["pricing_status"] = rp["status"]
        store["pricing_body"] = (rp.get("body") or "")[:60000]
    # 3 api-ish probes (budget: up to 8 total)
    used = len(recs)
    for path in ["/openapi.json", "/swagger.json"]:
        if used >= 8: break
        ra = get(urljoin(url_home, path), None)
        if ra["status"] == 200:
            store.setdefault("api_probe_hits", []).append({"path": path, "status": 200, "bytes": len(ra.get("body") or "")})
        used = len(recs)
    store["request_log"] = recs
    out = os.path.join(RAW, f"scan-{prefix}.json")
    json.dump(store, open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
    print(f"== {domain}: home={store['home_status']} robots={store['robots_status']} sitemap={store['sitemap_status']}({store['sitemap_loc_count']}) js={[(j['status'], j['bytes']) for j in store['js_fetched']]} pricing={store.get('pricing_status')} reqs={len(recs)}")
    return store

TARGETS = json.load(open(os.path.join(RAW, "_targets_batch.json")))
for t in TARGETS:
    try:
        run_target(t["domain"], t["url"], t["prefix"], t.get("js_max", 3))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"== {t['domain']}: EXCEPTION {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
print("BATCH DONE")

import os, re, json, gzip, time, ssl, urllib.request, urllib.error, socket
W = r"C:\Users\Garrett\.hermes\competitor-intel"
UA = {"User-Agent":"Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/126.0.0.0 Safari/537.36","Accept":"*/*","Accept-Encoding":"gzip, deflate"}
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(); ctx.check_hostname=False; ctx.verify_mode=ssl.CERT_NONE
def get(url, t=25):
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA), timeout=t, context=ctx) as r:
            d=r.read()
            if r.headers.get("Content-Encoding")=="gzip":
                try: d=gzip.decompress(d)
                except Exception: pass
            return r.status, r.geturl(), d
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, url, b""
    except Exception as e:
        return None, url, str(e).encode()

# 0) full scan1 for blockworks + brosonpm
s1 = json.load(open(os.path.join(W,"raw","batch3-scan1.json")))

bw=s1["blockworks.com"]["pages"]["home"]

title: Action Network: Sports Betting Odds, News & Analysis — part 2/2
body:
What Is Action Network?
Action Network is your go-to authority for sports betting, prediction markets, and casino gaming.
Since 2017, we've helped our readers make smarter, more informed decisions on their bets (and now trades). Tune in for industry-leading analysis, timely news coverage, real-time odds, professional-grade tools, and educational resources.
Why Choose Action Network?
We started as a sports betting authority, and that's still at our core — our experts have reviewed the best betting sites, built an award-winning Action Network App with unrivaled integrations like Playbook, and produced some of the best sports betting podcasts in the industry. That same rigor is why bettors have trusted us through every line, every game, and every season.
But the industry has evolved, and so have we. As prediction markets have grown into a major way to trade on sports and beyond, we've extended our same standard of expert analysis to platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket.
So whether you're betting or trading, you're getting the same trusted insight Action Network has always provided.
Sports Betting
From odds to analysis to bonuses, here's how Action Network helps you bet smarter on every sport.
Odds & Lines
We compare odds across sportsbooks so you always know where to find the best value, including on futures markets like the Super Bowl, March Madness, World Series, and Stanley Cup.
Our coverage spans every major league, including NFL, College Football, NBA, WNBA, College Basketball, NHL, and MLB. We also have experts specializing in other sports, including Golf, UFC/MMA, Tennis, NASCAR, Soccer, and College Baseball.
Tools
Our free and premium tools take the guesswork out of betting. Explore our wide range of betting calculators, weather trackers, injury reports, public betting data, and more to get an edge on your bets.
News
Stay current with breaking news across every league, plus updates on where sports betting stands in your state. Our sports betting legalization tracker and sportsbooks by state guide keep you informed as sportsbooks launch and legislation unfolds.
Analysis
Our experts break down matchups, share parlays, and deliver picks you can actually use. Expert picks for each league give you a second opinion before you lock in a bet.
Reviews & Promos
We review sportsbook apps so you know which ones are not only licensed in your state but also compatible with your betting preferences. We also break down valid promo codes for each, so you can claim valid welcome offers and understand how to make the most of your bonus bets. Check out the top sportsbooks and promos from: Fanatics Sportsbook, BetMGM, bet365, DraftKings, FanDuel, theScore Bet, betPARX, and Hard Rock Bet.
We even offer catch-all reviews specific to each league! For instance, check out these college football betting promos and NFL betting promos.
Education
New to betting, or just want to sharpen your edge? Our sports betting education hub covers everything from the basics to how to leverage expert picks and find value on your own.
Prediction Markets
Prediction markets let you trade on real-world outcomes — here's how Action Network helps you navigate them.
Tools & Pricing
Our odds comparison tools now include prediction market pricing, so you can compare between exchanges (such as Kalshi against Polymarket).
Our tools also let you weigh a prediction market price against a sportsbook line. And our dedicated prediction market odds calculator helps you understand contract pricing before you trade.
News
We track market-moving news as it happens to help you understand how current events affect prices. We also report on the regulatory and legalization updates that shape where and how prediction markets can operate. As this space rapidly evolves, our team stays on top of every ruling and policy shift.
Analysis
Action Network's experts weigh in on which markets are worth trading. Our prediction market analysis has a rigor similar to that of our sports betting analysis but is adapted for the unique landscape of event contract trading. By considering contract pricing, market sentiment, and the latest news, we publish picks you can continue to count on.
Reviews & Promos
We review prediction market apps so you know which platforms are user-friendly and CFTC-regulated.
We also break down prediction market promo codes so you can make the most of your trading credits and other rewards. The Polymarket promo code and Kalshi promo code are two of the top bonuses we recommend claiming.
If you want guides specific to each league, we've got 'em! Find the best NFL prediction market promos and college football prediction promos.
Education
Action Network publishes tons of advice on how to navigate the emerging space of prediction markets. We teach you how to fund your account, read contract prices, place trades, and more.
Casino
We track the best online casinos month by month, review social casinos and sweepstakes casinos, and maintain running lists of no-deposit bonus codes and welcome offers as operators change them.
On the land-based side, Action Network follows new property openings, licensing decisions, and expansions from Bally's Chicago to tribal and regional markets.
Ready to start? Our Fanatics Casino promo code page covers one of the better current offers.
Other iGaming Products
Prediction markets have reshaped not only sportsbooks but also other parts of the iGaming industry. Due to evolving consumer interests and regulatory hurdles, products such as DFS platforms and social sportsbooks have taken a backseat.
That being said, Action Network hasn't forgotten about the little guys. We remain an authority on DFS apps such as DraftKings Pick6, Dabble, Bleacher Nation Fantasy, and Betr.
We also review social sportsbooks, including Rebet, Thrillzz, and PlayBracco.

Method
GET/POST api.api-tennis.com/tennis/?method=get_news
Returns AI-synthesized tennis news articles about players, tournaments and matches. Available on the Ultra plan only.
An article is linked to every entity it's actually about — a single article can carry a player_key, a tournament_key and an event_key all at once (e.g. a match report is tied to the match itself, the tournament it's part of, and the featured player). Any of these three can independently be null if that dimension wasn't identified for the article. entity_type / entity_key are kept for backwards compatibility and just mirror the single most specific match reflected (priority: match > tournament > player).

Method
GET/POST api.api-tennis.com/tennis/?method=get_draw
Returns the tournament draw (bracket) for a given tournament and season - rounds, matchups, seeds and byes, plus each match's live result/status where already available. When the tournament's official draw has been published by our data provider, the response reflects that draw exactly ("source": "draw_feed"), including still-undecided future rounds as empty "TBD" slots that fill in automatically as each round is played. For tournaments where the official draw isn't available yet, the bracket is instead reconstructed from played/scheduled matches ("source": "reconstructed_from_results").

# HOW RATELIMIT WORKS

June 12, 2026 \- Posted in
[General](https://www.api-football.com/news/category/general) by
[API-SPORTS](https://www.api-football.com/news/author/api-sports)

Mastering rate limiting is essential to ensure the stability of our APIs, their optimal performance, and fair usage for everyone. In this context, a dedicated proxy layer plays a central role by precisely orchestrating traffic regulation. This article explains how the system works, how the queuing logic behaves, how 429 errors are generated, and which best practices to follow to avoid being blocked.

## **Subscription plans and limits**

Every access to our APIs is subject to a per‑minute rate limit, depending on the chosen plan:

- Free plan: 10 requests per minute.
- Pro plan: 300 requests per minute or 5 requests per second.
- Ultra plan: 450 requests per minute or 7 requests per second.
- Mega plan: 900 requests per minute or 15 requests per second.
- Custom plan: 1200 requests per minute or 20 requests per second, for custom plans up to 1.5 million requests per day.

If you need a higher volume, you can contact us via the dashboard chat so we can discuss a suitable configuration.

## **Rate limit headers**

When you use the API, the following headers are added to each response:

- `x-ratelimit-requests-limit`: number of requests allocated per day according to your subscription.
- `x-ratelimit-requests-remaining`: number of remaining requests for the current day.
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: maximum number of allowed calls per minute.
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: number of remaining calls before reaching the per‑minute limit.

These headers allow you to adapt your client‑side logic and better spread your calls over time.

## **Per user and per IP limits**

It is important to note that rate limiting is applied per user and per API, according to the limits defined by your subscription. In addition, the protection also takes into account the IP address used to make the calls.

In practice, this means that rate‑limit behavior depends both on your API key and on your source IP. If several users or services share the same public IP, their requests can be counted together from the network protection point of view, which may reduce your effective capacity more quickly.

For this reason, it is not recommended to call the API from environments where outbound IPs are shared among many different users. This can be the case for some managed or serverless services such as Cloudflare Workers, AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, Google Cloud Functions, Firebase Functions, Vercel Functions, Netlify Functions, as well as other comparable serverless or PaaS platforms.

Whenever possible, it is better to use a dedicated static IP so you keep full control over your traffic and avoid having another user on the same IP trigger protections that also affect your calls.

## **Orchestration with a dedicated proxy**

A dedicated proxy layer orchestrates the rate‑limiting process by turning subscription limits into a simpler processing rate. For example, if a user is on the Mega plan with a limit of 900 requests per minute, this layer converts it into an operational rate equivalent to 15 requests per second.

As long as the user stays below this threshold, rate limiting remains inactive and interactions with the API behave normally, without any particular constraint.

In the image below, the 15 requests received within the same second are processed immediately, because they stay within the limit allowed by the user’s plan:

![enter image description here](https://www.api-football.com/public/img/news/rate-1.jpg)

## **Moderate exceeding: queuing requests**

With the same example of a Mega plan allowing 15 requests per second, if a user sends 18 requests, the proxy immediately processes the first 15 and puts the remaining 3 on hold, to process them sequentially as soon as a new slot becomes available.

In other words, these extra requests are temporarily paused and then executed as soon as the traffic goes back under the threshold of 15 requests per second.

This queuing mechanism, called burst, makes it possible to briefly absorb a small overload without immediately rejecting calls.

The image below illustrates this case: the first requests are accepted immediately, while the following ones are delayed and then processed as soon as a slot becomes available:

![enter image description here](https://www.api-football.com/public/img/news/rate-2.jpg)

## **Exceeding the limit and 429 errors**

If a user exceeds the allowed rate to a point where the burst mechanism can no longer absorb it, rate limiting fully kicks in.

In the example below, 23 requests are sent: the first 15 are processed immediately, the next 5 are queued to be executed as soon as a slot is free, but the last 3 are rejected.

The next image shows exactly this situation, with three visible categories:

![enter image description here](https://www.api-football.com/public/img/news/rate-3.jpg)

For rejected requests, the API returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests error.

Example of a 429 response:

```
{
    "get": "",
    "parameters": [],
    "errors": {
        "rateLimit": "Too many requests. You have exceeded the limit of requests per minute of your subscription."
    },
    "results": 0,
    "paging": {
        "current": 1,
        "total": 1
    },
    "response": []
}
```


[... middle omitted — see footer ...]

- Slow down immediately when a 429 error appears.

## Conclusion

Rate‑limit management with a dedicated proxy layer is a delicate balance between ease of use, infrastructure protection, and fairness between users. The system can absorb small spikes thanks to burst, while rejecting or blocking usage that exceeds plan thresholds over time.

It is also important to remember that rate‑limit behavior depends not only on your subscription and your API key, but also on the IP used to make calls. For production integrations, using a dedicated static IP remains the best way to avoid side effects caused by shared IPs.

Finally, if none of our standard plans or their associated limits match your needs, you can contact us directly via the dashboard chat to set up a custom service. For the full policy and up‑to‑date information, please refer to the official documentation.

Seamlessly integrate with your stack

Choose from our growing ecosystem of integrations for data ingestion, visualization, language clients, and more.

Why is ClickHouse so fast?

Column-oriented databases are better suited to OLAP scenarios. They are at least 100x faster in processing most queries. ClickHouse uses all available system resources to their full potential to process each analytical query as fast as possible.

Row-oriented databases

In row-oriented databases, data is stored in rows, with all the values related to a row physically stored next to each other.

Column-oriented databases

In column-oriented databases, like ClickHouse, data is stored in columns, with values from the same columns stored together.

Read more in the docs ->->

Deploy your way

Unlike traditional closed-source databases, ClickHouse runs in every environment, whether it’s on your machine or in the cloud.

FAQs

Wherever you need us, we’re there. We love to engage in thoughtful conversation with the ClickHouse community and are always on-hand to answer your questions.

Ask us anything ->->

01

ClickHouse is faster than most traditional data warehouses and databases and is most often used when real-time queries on large datasets are necessary at an affordable cost. However, developers also often use ClickHouse on top of their CDWH or OLTP databases to act as a “speed layer” within their existing infrastructure.

02

OLAP stands for “online analytical processing” which contrasts from OLTP, or “online transaction processing.” As the name suggests, OLAP databases perform significantly better compared to OLTP databases for analytical workloads common with large datasets.

03

In order to easily process large amounts of data, ClickHouse uses highly optimized compression techniques and vectorized query execution to maximize CPU efficiency.

04

ClickHouse supports connectors to many clients and drivers, including common BI and data analysis tools. Please see this page for a complete list of supported integrations.

05

Self-managed ClickHouse is dependent on the cost of your compute and data storage resources, as well as headcount necessary to manage the ClickHouse deployment. For the most affordable way to run ClickHouse, use ClickHouse Cloud, which starts at $50/month.

Start using ClickHouse in seconds

body:
set -u
BASE="C:/Users/Garrett/.hermes/competitor-intel"
UA="Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/126.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
mkdir -p "$BASE/raw" "$BASE/dossiers"
for d in deepnewz.com defillama.com dexu.ai dimes.fi domeapi.io dune.com; do
  h=$(curl.exe -sL -m 25 -A "$UA" -o "$BASE/raw/$d.html" -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}" "https://$d/")
  echo "HOME $d :: $h :: bytes=$(wc -c < "$BASE/raw/$d.html")"
  r=$(curl.exe -s -m 15 -A "$UA" -o "$BASE/raw/$d.robots.txt" -w "%{http_code}" "https://$d/robots.txt")
  echo "ROBOTS $d :: $r"
done
for d in deepnewz.com defillama.com dexu.ai dimes.fi domeapi.io dune.com; do
  f="$BASE/raw/$d.html"
  echo "##### $d"
  echo "--TITLE--"; grep -oiE '<title[^>]*>[^<]{0,160}' "$f" | head -2
  echo "--APIURLS--"; grep -oE 'https?://[^"'"'"' <>\\]*api[^"'"'"' <>\\]*' "$f" | sort -u | head -25
  echo "--PATHS--"; grep -oE '"/(api|v[0-9])[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]{2,60}' "$f" | sort -u | head -25
  echo "--FRAMEWORK--"; grep -oE '_next/|__NEXT_DATA__|__NUXT__|nuxt|gatsby|svelte|angular|webpack|cdn-cgi|vercel|netlify|cloudflare|shopify|wordpres' "$f" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -12
  echo "--VENDOR--"; grep -oiE 'posthog|amplitude|segment\.io|mixpanel|datadog|sentry\.io|hotjar|clarity\.ms|googletagmanager|google-analytics|plausible|stripe|hubspot|intercom|crisp\.chat|matomo' "$f" | sort | uniq -ic | sort -rn | head -12
  echo "--PRICING--"; grep -ioE '.{0,45}(pricing|per month|/month|\$[0-9][0-9,]{1,9}).{0,45}' "$f" | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/  */ /g' | sort -u | head -15
done
echo "=====ROBOTSCONTENT====="
for d in deepnewz.com defillama.com dexu.ai dimes.fi domeapi.io dune.com; do
  echo "---robots $d---"; head -c 700 "$BASE/raw/$d.robots.txt" 2>/dev/null; echo
done

",e+='; 3) IPv6address does not work because of APG's "first-success disambiguation" and "greedy" repetitions.

",e+=";    That is SABNF instead of simple ABNF.
",e+='; 4) IPv4address fails because of "first-success disambiguation".
',e+=";    This could be fixed with rearrangement of the alternative terms. However, it would still not

Who it's for
Built for the people
running modern sports markets.
One pricing layer. Six audiences. A workflow tuned to each.

Professional Bettors & Syndicates
Where bettors who already win scale up. PRO Odds Screen surfaces every +EV play across 200+ books — sort by edge, hit lines before they move, and get more volume down across every account you run.

Sportsbook Operators & Trading Teams
Hang sharper prices. Detect line moves before competitors. Tighten margins at scale. Real-time True Line and steam alerts piped into your trading workflow — props, SGPs, alts, and main markets, all priced from one engine.

Market Makers, Exchanges & Prediction Markets
The pricing engine behind sharper numbers. Market makers hang lines, exchanges seed markets, and prediction markets price contracts — all off the same True Line that powers the PRO Odds Screen.

DFS & Sweepstakes Operators
Deep prop coverage and unified True Line pricing. Build fair contests, protect hold, and launch sports your current feed can't price.

Media & Affiliates
Coverage deep enough to monetize every page you run. Widget-ready odds across every sport, market, and book — the breadth to scale existing affiliate placements and open the ones your current feed can't price. Built for engagement, not just accuracy.

Professional Sports Teams
Player prop data, built for analytics teams. Project performance, model situational outcomes, and feed in-game decisions and game planning with the deepest prop market data in pro sports.

One stack. Every product.
The full Betstamp
data and pricing portfolio.
Five products, one data foundation — purpose-built for sharp bettors, sportsbooks, exchanges, and prediction markets across every layer of the modern sports market.

PRO Odds Screen
The odds screen built for sharp bettors and syndicates. True Line on every market, sub-second refresh, the deepest prop screen in the industry.
True Line pricing on every market and prop type
Sub-second refresh across 2,500+ markets
Side-by-side comparison against 200+ sportsbooks
See PRO Odds Screen →Talk to Sales

Sports Betting API
The deepest prop odds data set in the industry. REST + streaming, JSON-clean, full coverage from main lines to player props across 200+ books.

Sportsbook Pricing Feed
Power your book with proprietary True Line pricing across every market. Built for sportsbooks running pre-game and live trading at scale, with specialty prop and SGP pricing your in-house team can't match without doubling headcount.

Prediction Markets API
Full order book depth and live liquidity across every prediction market. Sub-second pricing across every contract, with no-fee pricing available.
SGP Pricing Engine
Same-game parlay fair value with multi-leg correlation modeling. Generates millions of correlated combinations with no manual adjustment required.

The methodology
The True Line: how we price the
sharpest props in the industry.
Our True Line model powers the products operators, professional bettors, and syndicates rely on when sharpest pricing is the requirement. Backtested on 5+ seasons of closing lines. Uniquely weighted against 200+ books. Tuned for the prop markets where most pricing fails.

01
Historical book efficiency
Each book weighted by sport, market, and prop type based on historical sharpness. Pinnacle's NBA spread isn't the same signal as their NFL alts.
02
Line move direction & timing
Sharp early action, steam moves, and reverse line movement all factored into how confidently each price gets set.
03
Bias correction by prop type
Player props, alts, and exotic markets carry structural biases the sides-and-totals world doesn't. We adjust per prop type.
04
Offshore + sharp-out reference set
More offshore and sharp-out reference books than any other provider — the books that move first when smart money lands.
See the True Line in Action →

Talk to a
 sports data expert.
Ready to get started? Book a demo and see the sharpest props pricing in the industry.
Talk to Sales →See PRO Odds Screen
